_global.note: STOP before doing WordPress-{state} selector work. Measured 2026-08-05 with scripts/find-duplicate-library-urls.js: 355 domains are shared across two or more ACTIVE states, covering 1073 of the ~4069 configured library entries. The seed data was generated by guessing '{city}library.org' from the city name, so madisonlibrary.org is assigned to libraries in 11 states, greenvillelibrary.org in 10, franklinlibrary.org in 10. A domain can be the real site of at most one of them. Until the URLs are corrected, a scraper returning 0 events may simply be pointed at another state's library — and broadening extraction would ingest that other library's events under the wrong name and state. Fix URLs before selectors. General discipline: read SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl first, verify claims before acting, run `node -c` on every modified scraper, and append one line per logical fix to SCRAPER-FIX-LOG.jsonl. SECOND SEED-DATA DEFECT, measured 2026-08-05: the same generator also fabricated county names by appending ' County' to the city ('Arcadia County', 'Brandon County', 'Archer County' -- none are real counties). Across the 20 active WordPress-{state} library files, 2065 of 2137 county values (96.6%) fail getCountyCentroid() lookup; only 72 resolve. Worst: NY 416 bad, MA 231, PA 206, NJ 166; VT/TN/KY/MS/WV are 100% bad. Effect: the county-centroid tier of the geocoding chain is effectively dead for this entire family, so any library whose address/city geocode fails lands on the STATE centroid. This is the same class of work as the URL remediation and needs a real city-to-county data source -- do not guess counties one at a time. That is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, so they are deliberately NOT marked DEAD: a timeout can be transient, geo-blocked, or firewalled against this sandbox in particular, and both the dns.resolve4 sweep and the ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT episode were cases of a failed probe being misread as a fact about the world. Retry them from a different network before concluding anything. Everything else is settled: 402 entries are guarded, and the remediation is a RISK reduction rather than a URL correction — each guarded library is now an explicit, uncovered gap that keeps its row in LIBRARY-SITE-AUDIT.md. NEXT AFTER DEFECT A — PLATFORM MISMATCHES, opened 2026-08-23, worklist in reports/platform-mismatches.md. Re-fetching them is pointless — the page really does show no events to a DOM reader. The productive question is WHY, and scripts/detect-site-platform.js answers it: of the 152 unverifiable sites that matched a live WordPress-{state} config entry, 40 are running a platform this codebase ALREADY PARSES (7 Assabet, 6 Google Calendar, 5 LibCal, 5 The Events Calendar REST, 4 BiblioCommons, 3 CivicPlus, 2 Communico, 1 LibraryMarket, plus 7 on LibraryAware which is a newsletter tool with no calendar to scrape). Every one of those can only ever return 0 where it currently sits, and the fix is RELOCATION to the right family, never selector work. A further 24 are seed-data problems in disguise — off-host, parked or empty URLs that never collided with another state and so never showed up in gate 2. Read the file's Method section before acting: a platform marker proves the platform is REFERENCED, not that it holds that library's events, so confirm the feed carries real dated events before moving any entry.

AGE-YEARPAIR-MISREAD.note: NOT a registry scraper — a cross-cutting finding kept visible in the Fix queue. OPEN, ongoing deletion of children's events. Distinct from the resolveAgeRange 'Adults' fix that landed 2026-08-13: that one gave a supplied 'Adults' a second opinion from the title and rescued 285 wrongly-deleted event instances, but it CANNOT rescue this class because the title itself yields no valid non-adult signal. Symptom: a title containing a YEAR PAIR or similar numeric pair is read as an age range, resolves to Adults, and the event is deleted. Largest known victim is '2026-27 KidsPlex After-School (Pay-by-Day Option)' with 82 rejected instances in scraper-stdout.log — a school-year label 2026-27 parsed as ages 26-27. This is the same family of false positive CLAUDE.md already documents for registration IDs ('2608-2026' read as 8-20) and times ('1:00 - 2:30p' read as 0-2), which is why normalizeAgeRange must never be fed a raw title. The remaining gap is that a numeric pair reaching detectAgeRange/normalizeAgeRange through a SUPPLIED value is still trusted. Suggested direction, NOT yet implemented or verified: reject an age range parsed from a pair that looks like a year or school year (both parts >= 1900, or a 4-digit first part, or a YYYY-YY shape) before it can normalize to Adults. Measure first — run the 320 distinct titles in scraper-stdout.log through any candidate change and check both directions, since the 968 not-rescued instances are a MIXED bag containing genuinely adult events (Coffee & Conversation, 3D Printer Orientation) that must stay rejected. Extend scripts/test-age-detection.js with the year-pair cases plus adult controls before shipping.

NONFAMILY-GUARD-BYPASS.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-24 — root cause found, closed at save time, and the 12 surviving rows deleted. THE MECHANISM WAS TWO GUARDS FAILING TOGETHER, which is why reading either one in isolation looked correct. (1) isNonFamilyEvent() DOES match the 18+ pattern, but it is cancelled by FAMILY_RESCUE_PATTERNS — and the CivicRec scraper AUTO-GENERATES a description ending "Family-friendly program in <city>, <ST>." for every row it emits, so every CivicRec event rescues itself from every non-family rule by construction. (2) The adult-only guard never fired because detectAgeRange() could not read an open-ended "Ages 18+" and the row resolved to All Ages. Neither guard was broken; each was individually defeated. FIXED by the same-day ages N+ rule: the exact live row now rejects as adult-only, verified by replaying its real name AND real description through flattenEvent. A SEPARATE PIPELINE HOLE WAS FOUND AND IS NOW CLOSED, and it was circular: fix-all-data-quality.js only deletes rows whose STORED age_range is already Adults, so it could never see these (stored All Ages); backfill-age-range.js re-derives correctly, spots them, then deliberately declines to act and advises running fix-all-data-quality.js, which cannot reach them. Each deferred to the other, so the rows were unreachable by both. Added scripts/purge-adult-gated-rows.js to close it, deliberately NARROWER than "is this adult": title-only, an explicit numeric gate required, the shared detectAgeRange() must independently agree, family-shaped titles rescued, and a ceiling that aborts. That narrowness is evidence-driven — of the 11 rows backfill flagged in a 20k sample, 8 were flagged from the DESCRIPTION and were ordinary listings (Delaware Korean Festival, Music in the Park, Fall Plant Sale), so deleting on that signal would have destroyed real content. backfill-age-range.js was RIGHT to refuse. Ran it over all 125,992 rows: 12 deleted, 0 false positives, 0 rescued, and a re-run reports 0 — Abington Fest 5K x3, Age 50+ Annual Membership x3, Adult age 19+ x3, Registration Ages 18+ x2, Game Night Out ages 18+ x1. STILL OPEN AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: those triplicates mean the same event re-inserted under a new id on three rotations. Since name+venue+description were identical and the DB unique-content index did NOT block them, the differing field must be event_date — which may be legitimate (a recurring listing whose date advances) rather than an id defect. Not proven either way; do not cite this as an id bug without checking event_date first. See the WordPressTec-Parks note for the same unresolved shape.

RECDESK-RESERVATIONS.note: OWNER DECISION NEEDED - RecDesk sites feed FIELD RESERVATIONS into a family-events product, and this is what makes gate 5 look like an age-detection regression every third day. RecDesk-Parks scrapes {slug}.recdesk.com/Community/Calendar, which on some slugs is the grounds-booking calendar rather than the programs catalog. Measured 2026-08-27 on RecDeskParks-ccrec: 3,706 rows, 992 of the first 1,000 tagged All Ages, and the most common titles are WRC Soccer - soccer field 3 (Mayeski Field 3 Softball with MP Overlay), WRC softball - coordinating with baseball, and Rugby (Bark Hill Field 2). Those are not events a parent can attend and they carry no age because they are not programs. Fleet effect: on 08-19, 08-22 and 08-25 the audit reads 13-18 percent specific, entirely because RecDeskParks-ccrec/lcncpr/westhartford/wheeling ran at 1-3 percent; on MacaroniKid-heavy days it reads 49-56 percent. A TITLE FILTER WAS BUILT, MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED: a broad parenthesised-facility predicate matched 42.5 percent of all 18,278 RecDeskParks rows but produced 845 FALSE POSITIVES that are real youth programming - 2026 Youth NFL Flag Football (Ages 10-12), Flag Football 5th-8th grade, Small-Sided Soccer 8-12 yrs - so shipping it would have deleted genuine family events. Narrowing to unambiguous grounds-coordinator language (coordinating with, MP overlay) is clean, zero false positives, but catches only 603 of ccrec 3,706 rows, so it fixes 16 percent while leaving the same junk in place and adding a special-case regex to maintain. THE REAL FIX IS THE ENDPOINT, not the title text or the age detector: point affected slugs at the programs/activities catalog instead of the community calendar. That is an owner-level call because it changes what an entire scraper family returns, and on some slugs the Calendar endpoint does carry real programs (Kindermusik, Beginner Gymnastics, Puddle Jumpers all came from it), so a blanket switch could LOSE coverage.
